To determine the number of workers needed, we must first calculate the effective capacity required per worker after accounting for the spike reserve, and then divide the total load by that effective capacity.

### Step 1: Calculate Effective Capacity per Worker

Each worker has a base capacity of 20 requests per second. However, 25% of this capacity must be reserved for spikes. This means only 75% of the worker's capacity is available for regular traffic.

$$
\text{Effective Capacity per Worker} = \text{Base Capacity} \times (1 - \text{Reserve Percentage})
$$

$$
\text{Effective Capacity per Worker} = 20 \times (1 - 0.25)
$$

$$
\text{Effective Capacity per Worker} = 20 \times 0.75 = 15 \text{ requests per second}
$$
